Sorry, do you know what is happening? I was in security when they announced the change.
Third gate tonight. I was sitting at eighteen when they moved us to thirty-four.
Thirty-four? I did not even hear that one. What were you doing when they announced it?
Eating, of course. I looked up and everybody was walking in the other direction.
That is how I found out about this one. Nobody was answering at the desk.
They gave out food vouchers about an hour ago. Did you get one?
No. I was still standing in the queue at the other gate.
Go and ask now. They are still giving them out, but only to the people who ask.
Sorry, do you know what is happening?
I was standing in the queue when they announced it.
While I was waiting, they changed the gate twice.
Nobody was answering at the desk.
Excuse me, is the airline giving out food vouchers?

The worst night I ever had at that desk, I was calling the operations centre every ten minutes and getting exactly the same answer as the passengers were getting from the screen. Nothing. While I was on the phone, a crowd was forming in front of me, and I could see it growing in the reflection of the window behind them. People shout at the person at the desk, and I understand why, but they are shouting at somebody who knows precisely as much as they do. I am not hiding anything. Nobody has told me either. The one thing I wish more passengers knew is this. After a certain number of hours, the airline has to give you food, and after more hours, sometimes a hotel. We do not announce it, because if we announced it to two hundred people at once we would have a riot. So people who ask, get it. Please ask.

I was sleeping on the floor near the window, with my bag under my head, when the flight was finally cancelled. I did not hear the announcement at all. What woke me up was a woman I had never spoken to, who was shaking my shoulder and telling me to go to the desk, because they were giving out hotel rooms and there were about forty left. I ran. I got one of the last ones. Six or seven people who were sleeping in the same corner as me did not, and they spent the night on that floor. Nothing separated us except that somebody woke me up. That is the thing I took from that night, and I have used it in airports ever since: the information is almost never announced to everybody. Somebody at a desk knows it, a few people ask, and the rest sleep on the floor.
